about.title: Montebello Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a car part gives out near the SR-60, a household appliance malfunctions, or a tool breaks during ordinary use. Montebello residents who are hurt this way often don't realize California law gives them a real path forward. Under the state's strict liability framework, you generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This can apply to a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a failure to warn about a known risk. Multiple parties along the supply chain, from manufacturer to retailer, may share responsibility. If a product hurt you or someone you love in Montebello, our team evaluates these cases at no upfront cost, so you can focus on recovering while we look at the legal side.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, the focus is on the product's condition, not the manufacturer's intent — our team knows how to build that kind of case.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share liability, which means we can help identify every avenue for recovery.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Matters Early
items.desc: Since the product itself is often central evidence, contacting us quickly can help ensure it's preserved before it's lost, repaired, or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving carelessness. Our team can review your situation to explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if possible, including any packaging or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or discard it, since the product itself is often key evidence. Store it somewhere safe until our team can advise you.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product near Whittier Boulevard in Montebello — does location matter?
items.answer: The location of your injury doesn't change the underlying product liability laws, but local details like where you purchased the product or where the incident occurred can be relevant to your claim. Our team can walk through the specifics with you at no cost.
